altitude.quote: at an altitude of 2630 m above sea level

coordinates.note: The Milagro collaboration states the detector position to 0.01 degrees (about 1 km). No detector or facility source fetched gives the pond position more precisely, so this is a site-level point with a 600 m half-width, not a surveyed detector coordinate (A23).
coordinates.quote: The detector was located at 106.68o W longitude, 35.88o N latitude in northern New Mexico at an altitude of 2630 m above sea level

name: Fenton Hill, Milagro site
notes: The point is the Milagro collaboration's published detector position given to 0.01 degrees.

summary.plain: The mountain site in the Jemez Mountains of northern New Mexico, run by Los Alamos National Laboratory, where the Milagro water pond observed TeV gamma rays and cosmic rays from 1999 to 2008.
summary.technical: Fenton Hill site of Los Alamos National Laboratory, about 35 miles west of Los Alamos, at 2630 m altitude (750 g/cm2); location of the Milagro water-Cherenkov observatory.
